title: perf(canary): automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Asha Raman
description: Motivation: intermittent and subtle latency/throughput regressions are the largest source of customer-facing incidents for inference workloads. This PR implements an automated performance canary pipeline that continuously evaluates per-model and per-route latency and throughput, detects statistically significant regressions, and blocks rollouts via rollout guards when impact exceeds configurable thresholds. What this contains: - New canary controller that runs lightweight synthetic load tests against a small fraction of traffic and compares recent distributions to historical baselines using bootstrap-based hypothesis tests and EWMA smoothing. - A regression detector component with configurable metrics (p95/p99 latency, tokens/s throughput, tail latency stability) and configurable significance/impact thresholds (alpha, min_sample_size, minimum relative increase). - Rollout guard integration with our deployment orchestrator: canary failures will automatically pause automated rollouts and create an incident-triage task; teams can choose to auto-rollback or require manual approval. - A canary config UI surface change (console) to set per-service thresholds and a default policy for server-side autopause. - CI/eval harness: synthetic benchmark suite + deterministic replay harness that validates detectors against historical regression traces and known-good traces. - Backfill script to seed baselines from the last 90 days and migration to store baselines in the perf-canary indexed store. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for detector logic and bootstrap test coverage. - Integration tests: end-to-end run in perf-canary lab with mocked workloads and realtime aggregation. - Manual canary run against staging showing detection of an injected 12% p95 regression. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag perf_canary_auto_detect. - Rollout to a small subset of services in staging for 48h, then 10% of traffic for 72h in canary-enabled prod regions. - Monitor signals and enable auto-rollback for high-confidence failures only. Checklist: - [x] detector algorithms implemented and unit-tested - [x] canary controller and scheduling - [x] rollout guard integration + incident task creation - [x] console controls + default policy - [x] migration + baseline backfill script - [x] perf lab validation and measurement notes Related: ENG-2841 (perf-canary requirements), ENG-2910 (rollout automation). Notes: kept detector pipeline lightweight to avoid adding significant overhead to serving path; all heavy aggregation happens in the canary pipeline workers. Config defaults are conservative to reduce false positives; ops playbooks and a small runbook added in the Console docs.

release_notes: Adds automated performance canary detection and rollout guards. Default is behind feature flag. Operators can configure per-service thresholds and choose auto-rollback or manual approval. Includes migration to seed baselines.
testing_notes: Staging validation: detected injected 12% p95 regression and paused rollout; recovery path validated with auto-rollback on high-confidence failures. Perf lab logs at perf-canary/benchmarks/run-2026-02-20.tar.gz
risk_summary: Conservative defaults to limit false positives; detector uses EWMA smoothing and min sample size. Risk: misconfigured thresholds can cause unnecessary pauses; ops playbook added to handle overrides and manual rollouts.
migration_notes: Run migration perf-canary/migrations/0003_backfill_baselines.sql to seed 90d baselines; job scheduled as part of post-merge pipeline.
notes_for_release_engineering: Ensure helm values perfCanary.enabled = true and perfCanary.featureFlags.autoDetect = false for initial rollout. Coordinate baseline backfill before enabling autoDetect at scale.
